newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops, rebels battle it out in northeast.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops, rebels battle it out in northeast.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops, advancing into Tamil rebel territory, fought a pitched battle along one flank on Friday and consolidated their hold on a captured town along another, military officials said.

Military officials in the north told Reuters a column of troops advancing along the eastern flank met stiff resistance from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) near Nedunkeni, about 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya.
"There is heavy fighting going on around Nedunkeni. Close to a half a dozen Tigers are likely to have been killed in the battle," one official said.

Meanwhile, troops who advanced on another flank to capture the rebel-held town of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya, were consolidating positions on Friday, the fourth day of a major thrust into the rebels' northern Wanni heartland.
Two soldiers were killed near Omanthai on Friday by rebel mortars, which were being fired from Puliyankulam further north, military officials said.
Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte visited troops on the frontline on Friday morning and inspected the progress of the offensive, launched last Tuesday, they said.
Troops based in Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, backed by artillery, tanks and helicopter gunships, launched the offensive code-named "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory".

The Defence Ministry says the main aim of the drive is to capture areas in the shrub-covered Wanni region from the LTTE, who are waging a war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.

But analysts say the offensive aims to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya in north-central Sri Lanka with the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north. The peninsula's main town of Jaffna, capital of the rebels' would-be homeland, is under government control.
The military has been tight-lipped about where the troops are heading.
The LTTE's international spokesman in London accused the military on Thursday of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property under the guise of opening up a supply route.
Anton Raja said droves of civilians have abandoned their homes to seek shelter in the mosquito-infested jungle.
An international aid worker in Vavuniya told Reuters at least 10 civilians had been killed and more wounded in the artillery shelling of the Wanni.
The Defence Ministry said on Thursday that troops monitoring LTTE transmissions has confirmed that at least 100 rebels had been killed or wounded in the battle for Omanthai alone.
But the clandestine rebel Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in Vavuniya, said on Friday the LTTE had lost only six people in the four days of fighting. It did not say how many were wounded.
Army casualties in Omanthai and elsewhere stood at 18 dead and 31 wounded in the first three days of the offensive, the Defence Ministry said.
But military sources said about 80 soldiers had been wounded since the offensive began, some of them seriously.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is higher.
